notes: smbclient/smbmap list shares; try a null session. Getting-Started intro - Module 04's enum4linux-ng/rpcclient go deeper.
name: SMB - Share Enumeration (Getting Started)
description: List SMB shares (-N null session, -L list) then connect to interesting ones as guest or with credentials to pull files.

defense.why_it_works: SMB shares may allow null sessions or unauthenticated guest access, exposing files that contain sensitive data including credentials. Some SMB versions are vulnerable to RCE exploits such as EternalBlue.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to SMB (TCP 445/139); a null/guest session or valid credentials for authenticated enumeration.
defense.impact: A list of shares and readable files — often exposing credentials or sensitive data — plus the server version for CVE matching (e.g. EternalBlue).
defense.detection: [MITRE T1135 AN0513] Process or script enumerates network shares via CLI (net view, net share, PowerShell Get-SmbShare/WMI) or OS APIs (NetShareEnum, srvsvc.NetShareEnumAll RPC) → bursts of outbound SMB/RPC connections (port 445/139) to many hosts within a short window → optional follow-on file listing or copy operations.
defense.artifacts: SMB session-setup and tree-connect events (Windows 5140/5145 with share auditing enabled); a connection to 445 in network logs.
defense.prevention:
Enforce SMB signing — by default 'Message signing enabled but not required', which leaves sessions vulnerable to relay attacks. Require authentication for all shares, disable SMBv1, and audit share permissions to remove unnecessary access.

[MITRE T1135 M1028] Enable Windows Group Policy setting 'Do Not Allow Anonymous Enumeration of SAM Accounts and Shares' to limit which users can enumerate network shares. Enforce least-privilege access to shares so only authorized users can list them.
defense.misconfiguration: Common introductory misconfigurations: services running as root/SYSTEM unnecessarily, default credentials unchanged, unnecessary services listening on all interfaces, lack of firewall rules exposing services externally, no monitoring or alerting on authentication failures.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service listening on all interfaces with default creds (common in labs/staging):
ss -tlnp | grep LISTEN
# 0.0.0.0:21  (FTP on all interfaces)
# 0.0.0.0:3306 (MySQL on all interfaces — should be 127.0.0.1 only)
# 0.0.0.0:8080 (Tomcat with manager app accessible)

# Running services as root:
ps aux | grep -E '(mysql|apache|nginx|ftp)'
# root  1234  /usr/sbin/mysqld  <-- should run as 'mysql' user
defense.secure_config:
# Bind services to localhost or specific IPs (not 0.0.0.0):
# MySQL: my.cnf -> bind-address = 127.0.0.1
# Apache: Listen 127.0.0.1:80 (if behind a proxy)

# Run services as dedicated low-priv users:
# systemd unit: User=mysql Group=mysql

# Host-based firewall (ufw):
ufw default deny incoming
ufw allow from 10.10.1.0/24 to any port 22  # SSH from mgmt only
ufw allow 443  # HTTPS
ufw enable

# Change all default credentials immediately after installation
# Enable fail2ban for SSH and web services
